Jordan E. Cooper’s Oh Happy Day! is an achingly relevant play with gospel music that evokes ideology about divinity in a thrilling and fascinating way.
Cooper’s fascinating but flawed new show asks us to be present and to recognize the human frailty and the possibility of redemption in all of those around us.
No amount of skilled performance can rescue a play at war with itself.

cn.t: Cooper's gospel-infused Noah's Ark reimagining divides critics with its ambitious blend of family drama and biblical parable. The Divines' powerful musical numbers earn praise, but the script struggles with tonal shifts and narrative coherence.

vr.q: Oh Happy Day! is probably one of my favorite pieces I've ever seen at The Public.
